expected.natural_english: the silver lining — it could have been so much worse

expected.natural_english: to let go of expectations — want nothing, hurt less
expected.literal_gap: Literally “to empty the heart/mind”; in use, “to let go of expectations — want nothing, hurt less”.
Literally, “save the person!” In danger, this is a cry for help. It can also be exaggerated jokingly in an overwhelming situation.

expected.natural_english: high-maintenance — it takes a lot of care
expected.literal_gap: Literally, “the hand goes a lot”; in use, something takes a lot of care or work. 많이 describes how much the hand goes to the task, not a number of hands.

expected.natural_english: overnight — all at once, out of nowhere
expected.literal_gap: Literally “in one morning”; in use, “overnight — all at once, out of nowhere”.

expected.natural_english: utterly swamped — not a second to breathe

gloss.gloss: no gap to open eyes and nose

expected.literal_gap: Literally “no gap to open eyes and nose”; in use, “utterly swamped — not a second to breathe”.

expected.natural_english: Running late (the dated or joking expression “Korean time”).
expected.literal_gap: Literally, “Korean time”; in dated or joking usage, this refers to lateness. It is not a claim that Koreans are generally late or a literal time-zone name.
